name: Turismo EP
licence_quote: No Copyright. The person who associated a work with this deed has dedicated the work to the public domain by waiving all of his or her rights to the work worldwide under copyright law
source: procedural / physically modelled synthesis, curated by ear
licence_note: made for Dawsome from no recordings, by a physical model and effects of its own; dedicated CC0 1.0
notes: a tine electric piano made for Dawsome by a physical model, with no recordings: a struck steel tine whose own overtones sit at a free bar's mode ratios and die fast (the bell of the attack), a tone bar that swells in and rings on, and a magnetic pickup's curve that the tine swings through; harder notes bark because the tine swings further into the pickup's field, not because of a filter

played through its own effects, baked into the samples: an EQ that thins the lows (-3 dB under 250 Hz) and lifts the middle (+6 dB around 1.2 kHz), a slow six-stage phaser (0.3 Hz, 200 Hz to 4 kHz), a deep slow two-voice chorus, a 1.85 Hz tremolo, the stereo sides 2 dB wider, light 1.5:1 compression and a short room (1.2 s decay, 10 ms predelay, 10 % wet) whose tail rings on after the note

31 notes on C, D, F, G and A from C1 to C7, each key playing its nearest note (keys 0-127); three velocity layers (1-42, 43-84, 85-127) played at velocities 40, 80 and 112, so harder is brighter as well as louder; one sample per note and layer
every sample peaks at -1 dBFS (true peak -0.5 dBTP at most); the default amp_veltrack=100 turns velocity into loudness; ampeg_release=0.25

each note is held until it dies away: its sample starts at the note's onset with a 0.25 ms fade-in, is high-passed at 15 Hz, and ends where its 10 ms level has fallen 63 dB under its peak for good, faded out over 5 ms (5.4 to 51.4 s; the low notes ring longest)

48 kHz stereo, rendered at 24 bits and stored as 16-bit FLAC: each sample dithered to 16 bits as y = rint(x * 32767 + a - b), clipped to 16 bits, where x is the render's 24-bit value over 2^23 and a, then b, are a frame-by-channel array of uniform noise on [0, 1) from NumPy's default_rng seeded with the first 8 bytes, big-endian, of the SHA-256 of the file's name without .flac, so the same render always gives the same 16-bit samples; each sample's MANIFEST.json entry names its render and that render's SHA-256 (member, made_from_sha256)
volume lowered by 0.20 dB so a full-velocity note peaks at or below -1 dBFS (its loudest note reaches -0.80 dBFS when resampled)
